subject: assumptions for link functions and distribution of latent variables in lavaan

messages.author: 1f4788b2494346da
messages.subject: assumptions for link functions and distribution of latent variables in lavaan
parts:
Hi,

I'm wondering if lavaan could be used for the following analysis:
I have data on "degree" (in this case the number of relationships formed in the past year) for about two hundred respondents (about 400 relationships), and whether or not condoms were used consistently in each of these relationships. The degree data seem distributed according to a negative binomial distribution.
Hence, I'd like to fit a model where I have one latent variable, let's call it "drive", which is gamma distributed; and each respondent's "drive" is the rate parameter of a Poisson process that governs the random variable "degree". Further I want to fit a regression model where this latent drive variable predicts consistent condom use (logit link function).

Many thanks in advance for your kind reply.
Best regards,

Wim Delva (Prof global health and HIV modelling, Ghent University)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: assumptions for link functions and distribution of latent variables in lavaan
parts:
On 09/24/2013 12:59 AM, Wim Delva wrote:

> Hence, I'd like to fit a model where I have one latent variable, let's
> call it "drive", which is gamma distributed; and each respondent's
> "drive" is the rate parameter of a Poisson process that governs the
> random variable "degree". Further I want to fit a regression model where
> this latent drive variable predicts consistent condom use (logit link
> function).

I'm afraid not. lavaan (0.5-14) only supports normally distributed
latent variables; and has only support for continuous, binary or ordered
observed variables, using a probit link function.

It would seem you need a custom programmed routine for this. I would
hunt down a local SAS/R guru for this.

Yves.
